test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 15 Sept 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Why was the use of 'kulhads' discontinued?

options.text: Use of clay resulted in the loss of the fertile top-soil

solution:
The correct answer is __**Use of clay resulted in the loss of the fertile top-soil**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Large-scale production **of **kulhads required significant amounts of clay**, which **often **came from the **top, fertile layer of soil**.
 
• This **removal of topsoil could negatively impact agricultural productivity** in the long run.
 
• **Kulhads **sometimes called a **shikora**, is a** traditional handleless pottery cup** from South Asia that is typically undecorated and unglazed, and is meant to be disposable.
 
• While kulhads have eco-friendly advantages, the depletion of fertile topsoil for mass production became a significant reason for their discontinuation, especially in trains where they were widely used.
 
• They are still used in some areas and efforts are being made to use them sustainably, like sourcing clay from non-agricultural land or using different production methods.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fertile top soil **has the following **characteristics**:

 
 
• It is **rich in nutrients** necessary for basic plant nourishment.
 
• This includes **nitrogen**, **phosphorus **and **potassium**.
 
• It consists of **adequate minerals **such as **boron**, chlorine, **cobalt**, copper, iron, **manganese**, magnesium, **molybdenum**, sulphur and **zinc**.
